rows.title: Bottoming Tap
rows.definition: A tap with a short chamfer, typically engaging one to one and a half threads before reaching full thread form, designed to cut threads as close as practical to the bottom of a blind hole.

general_taxonomy.fact: Incomplete internal threads are inherently present at the bottom of a tapped blind hole -- the physical reason bottoming taps exist as a distinct style.
general_taxonomy.source: NASA-STD-5020A section 4.7.5 [TFSR 25]: "Where blind holes are tapped, incomplete internal threads are present at the bottom of the hole."

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 1-2 threads/pitches, the shortest of the three chamfer-length tap styles.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

typical_applications.fact: Cannot start in an unthreaded hole; used to extend threads to the base of a blind hole after a taper and/or plug tap has already established the thread.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

rows.title: Forming Tap
rows.definition: A tap that forms threads by radially displacing material rather than cutting it, producing no chips; also referred to as a roll tap or fluteless tap.

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Requires a larger pre-tap hole diameter than an equivalent cutting tap, since material is displaced outward rather than removed.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

typical_applications.fact: Unsuitable for brittle materials such as cast iron, which can crack rather than flow under the forming pressure.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

typical_applications.fact: Produces no chips, which removes chip-evacuation as a constraint on blind-hole use -- unlike cutting taps, hole geometry (blind vs. through) is not the limiting factor for this tap type; material ductility is.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

manufacturer_specific_recommendations.fact: Requires a ductile workpiece material -- commonly cited minimum elongation of roughly 8% and maximum hardness of roughly Rc 30 -- because threads are formed by plastic displacement, not cutting.
manufacturer_specific_recommendations.source: Commonly cited across manufacturer/tooling technical guides (e.g. Harvey Performance, Jarvis Cutting Tools); not independently verified against a primary standard in this phase

rows.title: Hand Tap
rows.definition: A tap designed for manual operation with a tap wrench, typically supplied as part of a set spanning taper, plug, and bottoming chamfer styles for a given thread size.

typical_applications.fact: Designed for manual operation with a tap wrench; commonly supplied as a taper/plug/bottoming set for progressive blind-hole tapping by hand.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

rows.title: Plug Tap
rows.definition: A tap with a moderate chamfer length, shorter than a taper tap but longer than a bottoming tap, engaging approximately three to five threads before reaching full thread form.

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 3-5 threads/pitches, shorter than a taper tap and longer than a bottoming tap.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

typical_applications.fact: General-purpose tap; commonly the sole tap used for through-hole tapping, and can start in an unthreaded hole (unlike a bottoming tap).
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

rows.title: Spiral Flute Tap
rows.definition: A tap with helical (spiral) flutes that lift chips backward out of the hole entrance during cutting, commonly associated with blind-hole applications.

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Helical (spiral) flutes lift chips backward, up and out of the hole entrance, opposite in direction to a spiral-point tap.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

typical_applications.fact: Suited to blind-hole tapping, where chips cannot be pushed forward out of a closed bottom.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

rows.title: Spiral Point Tap
rows.definition: A tap with an angled point ground onto the flutes that pushes chips forward, ahead of the tap and out through the far side of the hole, commonly associated with through-hole applications.

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Also called a gun tap or gun-nose tap; a forward-angled point ground onto the cutting chamfer drives chips forward, ahead of the tap.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources (Cutwel, MisolTap, Slugger Tools)

typical_applications.fact: Suited to through-hole tapping only. In a blind hole the forward-pushed chips have nowhere to go, pack at the bottom, and can bind and break the tap.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources; consistent with NASA-STD-5020A's confirmation that blind-hole tapped threads terminate at a closed bottom with no chip escape path

rows.title: Taper Tap
rows.definition: A tap with a gradually tapered chamfer at the point, typically engaging six to eight threads before reaching full thread form, used to start threads gradually and reduce cutting force per pass.

manufacturing_characteristics.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 7-10 threads/pitches, the longest of the three chamfer-length tap styles.
manufacturing_characteristics.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources (Travers Tool, MisolTap, Rapmaf, AIMS Industrial)

typical_applications.fact: Long chamfer distributes cutting load gradually and makes the tap easier to start straight/square, but it cannot cut full-depth threads within roughly 7-10 pitches of the bottom of a blind hole.
typical_applications.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources
